page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The memory configuration includes 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an extensive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance comes bundled with 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and carries no discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarking, the D48ds_v7 registers top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.3 GB/sec and strong results across large-block uncached memory bandwidth, delivering 259.05 GB/sec read and 106.22 GB/sec write throughput. CPU testing reveals a PassMark CPU score of 68,963.55 and extended instruction execution scoring 61,853.85. Stress-ng scores settle in the middle 50% tier, showing 2,263.78 for single-core and 49,841.59 for multi-core throughput.

Workload testing highlights solid execution across caching, storage, and web serving, delivering 84.18 million Redis SET operations per second, 72.52 GB/sec of static web throughput, and strong database operation performance. Small-model LLM prompt processing achieves 2,691.32 tokens per second and 239.1 tokens per second on medium 7B models. The balanced compute, memory, and fast NVMe allocation provides balanced cost efficiency for enterprise caching tiers, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and database deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores running on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Configured with 192.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU) and a large 480 MB L3 cache, the system includes 2835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage without discrete graphics accelerators. Architectural flags support AVX-512, AMX, and accelerated cryptographic instructions. Synthetic and practical benchmarks reflect top-tier gzip compression alongside strong memory read/write throughput, high PassMark CPU extended instruction metrics, and elevated Redis SET rates exceeding 84 million operations per second. This hardware profile provides resource-dense throughput suited for enterprise databases, static web serving clusters, intermediate CPU-based machine learning inference, and distributed backend applications requiring fast local scratch storage.
